thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Futures Rise More Than 100 Points Amid Signs Of Thawing Trade Tensions

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Futures Rise More Than 100 Points Amid Signs Of Thawing Trade Tensions
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Tesla gains, Facebook lower in premarket trading
U.S. stock-index futures climbed Wednesday, with a multisession advance that has been inspired by a rally in technology and internet shares intact as investors followed developments in trade talks between Washington and key global partners and monitored Italy's political drama, which could have knock-on effects in the eurozone and undercut the recent market uptrend.
Read:Here's why Italy and financial markets are still headed for a showdown (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/italy-reminds-investors-to-sleep-with-one-eye-open-2018-06-05)
What are the markets doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 105 points, or 0.4%, to 24,926, while S&P 500 futures added 5.40 points, or 0.2%, to 2,757. Nasdaq-100 futures were up 10 points, or 0.1%, to 7,189.25.
On Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-edge-higher-with-techs-eyeing-a-new-record-2018-06-05), the Dow finished down less than 0.1% to 24,799.98, while the S&P 500 index rose less than 0.1% to 2,748.79. The Nasdaq Composite Index advanced 0.4% to 7,637.86, marking a second record close and the third consecutive advance for the tech-laden equity gauge.
The small cap-oriented Russell 2000 index ended near an all-time intraday top at 1,664.69 set at one point Tuesday.
Also read:First-half volatility sets stage for stock market's 'next leg higher,' says prominent bull (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/one-of-the-stock-markets-biggest-bulls-just-lifted-his-2018-sp-500-target-to-3200-2018-06-05)
What was driving the market?
Investors on alert for developments over the trade front may have gotten signs of a thaw after Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin reportedly urged President Donald Trump to exempt Canada from metals tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mnuchin-reportedly-urged-trump-to-exempt-canada-from-steel-aluminum-tariffs-2018-06-05) at a meeting Tuesday. That adds to a report Wednesday that China had offered to buy some $70 billion of U.S. goods to get the Trump administration to cool its tariff threats (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-offered-to-buy-nearly-70-billion-of-us-goods-2018-06-05).
Still, some tensions could still be simmering after Mexico revealed which U.S. products it is targeting for import tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mexico-details-retaliatory-tariffs-on-us-products-including-cheese-apples-bourbon-2018-06-05)--around $3 billion for goods including apples and bourbon--in retaliation for U.S. duties on Mexican steel and aluminum.
Leaders of the Group of Seven nations will likely discuss trade as they hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday. Tension between the U.S. and the six other members is expected, given the hostile reactions to tariffs imposed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/death-knell-for-the-g-7-may-be-at-hand-after-hostile-reaction-to-trump-tariffs-2018-06-04) by the Trump administration.
The Nasdaq Composite rallied 1.1% in the first two sessions of the week, while the Dow and S&P 500 have lagged behind, with gains of 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively. Gains for technology stocks have been driven by the belief among some that sector heavyweights such as Netflix Inc. (NFLX) and Apple Inc. (AAPL) can weather an economic pullback, if that happens.
But some market observers are worried that investor complacency may be setting in, (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-streets-fear-index-falls-to-more-than-4-month-low-as-tech-stocks-romp-2018-06-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-streets-fear-index-falls-to-more-than-4-month-low-as-tech-stocks-romp-2018-06-05) after the Cboe Volatility Index hit its lowest level since late January on Tuesday, falling 2.7% to 12.40.
Investors are breathing a little easier after signs of an effort on the trade front, said Konstantinos Anthis, head of research at ADS Securities, in reference to the reports about Mnuchin's Canada request and China's olive branch over U.S. goods.
"This news points toward an easing of geopolitical risks which paints a positive outlook for global growth and investors are jumping into the fray to benefit from this positive tilt in risk sentiment," said Anthis, in a note to clients.
"With the U.S. trade data released this afternoon, there is a certain weariness of the potential impact Donald Trump will have upon risk sentiment given his propensity to tweet around such events. With China attempting to stifle US tariffs, we are clearly at a crucial juncture for global trade, despite the relative optimism seen throughout global financial markets," said Joshua Mahony, market analyst at IG, in a note.
Which stocks were in focus?
Tesla Inc. (TSLA) shares rose 2.2% in premarket trading after CEO Elon Musk told shareholders that the electric-car maker was "quite likely" to meet its production goal of 5,000 Model 3 cars a week. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elon-musk-says-tesla-quite-likely-to-meet-model-3-production-goal-of-5000-a-week-2018-06-05)
Read:Tesla investors missed opportunity to hold Elon Musk & Co. accountable (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tesla-investors-missed-opportunity-to-hold-elon-musk-co-accountable-2018-06-05)
Also:Latest Wall Street view on Tesla is a cautious one (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/latest-wall-street-view-on-tesla-is-a-cautious-one-2018-06-01)
UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) shares rose 1% in premarket trade after the health care company raised its quarterly dividend by 20% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/unitedhealths-stock-rallies-after-boosting-dividend-20-setting-new-100-million-share-buyback-program-2018-06-06).
Facebook Inc.(FB) shares fell 0.8% in the premarket after the social-media giant confirmed it had shared user data with at least four Chinese tech companies (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-confirms-it-shared-user-data-with-chinese-tech-companies-2018-06-05). U.S. officials have warned that devices from one of those companies--Huawei Technologies Co.--could be exploited for state-sponsored spying.
Twitter Inc.(TWTR) shares fell 0.8% in premarket after announcing plans for an $1 billion convertible debt offering.
Signet Jewelers Ltd. shares (SIG) rose 2.8% in premarket trade Wednesday before reversing the gains, after the company beat estimates for its fiscal first quarter (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/signet-jewelers-tops-earnings-estimates-and-backs-guidance-2018-06-06) to May 5.
Shares of Axovant Sciences Ltd. (AXON) soared nearly 60% in premarket trade Wednesday, after Oxford BioMedica PLC(OXB.LN) said it has entered an $842.5 million licensing agreement (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/axovant-shares-soar-49-premarket-on-8425-mln-licensing-pact-for-parkinsons-treatment-2018-06-06) for OXB-102, a gene therapy treatment for Parkinson's disease.
What's on the economic calendar?
Data on the trade deficit for April is due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, along with readings on productivity and unit labor costs for the first quarter.
Opinion:A new economic indicator is saying there is no sign of a U.S. recession (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/a-new-economic-indicator-is-saying-theres-no-sign-of-a-us-recession-2018-06-05)
See:MarketWatch's economic calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks finished mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-makes-up-early-losses-as-asian-markets-are-mostly-quiet-2018-06-05). The Stoxx Europe 600 index was wobbling, with Italian stocks reversing gains and moving lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-wobble-as-ecb-officials-signal-qes-end-is-up-for-discussion-2018-06-06)after European Central Bank officials hinted policy makers will begin to focus on ending the central bank's bond-buying program.
The ICE U.S. Dollar Index dipped 0.2% to 93.728, with the greenback pushing lower chiefly against the euro and the Aussie dollar .
Read: Exports drive Australia's GDP surge (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/exports-drive-australias-gdp-surge-2018-06-06)
The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note was up 3.8 basis points to 2.949%, after falling to (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/treasury-yields-tick-lower-ahead-of-economic-data-2018-06-05) 2.917% late Tuesday, according to FactSet.
U.S. crude prices slipped 0.3% to $65.27 a barrel. Gold (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-continues-to-languish-below-1300-2018-06-05) was off 0.2% at $1,298.70 an ounce.
